However, instead of dismissing the plea today, a Bench of Justices PS Narasimha and Alok Aradhe gave Matrimony.com and Jodi365 an opportunity to explore an amicable resolution. Matrimony.com offered to rename its application “Jodi Matrimony” to avoid abruptly shutting down the business and affecting its existing users. items.title: Kerala: Clip from play on Emergency-era torture circulated as obscene, actor reacts
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. A Malayalam play titled Misa, staged as part of the Democratic Youth Federation of India’s (DYFI) 16th state conference in Thrissur, has triggered a controversy after certain scenes were recorded and misrepresented on social media. DYFI is the youth wing of the Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)], and Misa was conceptualised and performed by Chilanka Floating Theatre, a Kozhikode-based theatre group. The play tells the story of Snehalata Reddy, an artist who faced state torture during the Emergency in 1975, touching upon political oppression, exploitation of workers, and the suppression of dissent during that period. The title Misa is a take on the now repealed Maintenance of Internal Security Act (MISA), which gave the government enormous powers to detain individuals. The controversy began after social media profiles linked to the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), Congress, and Sangh Parivar circulated the clip of a particular scene from the play, depicting the custodial torture Snehalata endured. Sanjush was allegedly driving an Aston Martin at a high speed when the car hit Bharati Mukhi, a sales associate at a Lifestyle store in the Inorbit Mall in Madhapur, Hyderabad. Bharati was crossing the road while bringing lunch from a place nearby and returning to work, according to the complaint filed by the store manager Aswin Kumar. Madhapur ACP Ch Sridhar said Sanjush was not arrested because the offence registered against him is bailable and carries a maximum punishment of less than seven years. items.title: Telangana CM Revanth Reddy denied permission by MEA to visit USA
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. Telangana Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy has been forced to cancel the US leg of his overseas tour after the Ministry of External Affairs denied political clearance for his visit, stating that “clearance from political angle is denied”. CM Revanth, who is currently in London, will now return to Hyderabad on August 23 instead of travelling to Boston and New York. His original itinerary included a visit to New York, where he was scheduled to attend an Indian Overseas Congress meet-and-greet. He was expected to return to Hyderabad on August 30. The Telangana government had sought the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) led Union government’s approval for the Chief Minister’s visits to both the UK and the US in accordance with established protocol. While permission was granted for the UK leg, clearance for the US visit was withheld. The decision was conveyed to the state government after the official delegation had already reached the UK.
